The other adverse effect given in DES 72-62 p.28 is 2) the economies of areas near department lands were ORV use takes place. To this I would like to present the following observation made at the Brown County State Park on the State level. The park is at present overused by campers, while private camp grounds, abundant in Brown County (and one of the only means of income in an area, that has to rely on the tourist dollar) are having a hard time competing with the lower prices inside the park area. If the park were closed to campers the economy of the area would go up, the cost would be taken off the taxpayer's shoulder who has to pay for the overuse by excessive maintenance cost and would place it onto the camper-user. The same would hold true for the ORV industry. Tourism is very definitely an industry and should be placed entirely into the private sector and financed by those who engage in the different recreational uses.
There are many other perfectly legitimate recreational uses beginning with golf, swinning, baseball etc. that are not financed out of federal funds and accomplated on public lands as 0 % users are desiring in the case of establishing and maintaining expansive trails.
